blind_spots.blind_spot: FeaturePrint verification assumes a live registry connection wherever the part is checked
blind_spots.operator_reality: A munitions depot floor, forward arming point, or flight line is DDIL by default — the verify-photo has nowhere to send its match query, so the authentication step silently becomes optional exactly where counterfeit parts matter most. Same failure mode as the 30fps crowd-detection case: the architecture assumes bandwidth the environment denies.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their commercial anchor markets (luxury goods, pharma, datacenters) always have connectivity; specialties list 'cloud computing' as a core competency and nothing on the site mentions offline or edge matching.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: At any point in the value chain, take another photo. FeaturePrint matches it with >99.9% accuracy and zero false positives.

blind_spots.blind_spot: The 'any mobile phone' capture workflow collides with DoD device policy and field capture conditions
blind_spots.operator_reality: Personal phones are banned in SCIFs, munitions storage, and most sensitive maintenance areas; the E-5 doing the check is on a GFE device that needs an ATO'd app — and is photographing a corroded, greasy, dust-covered part in gloves, not a clean item in a fixture. Their own demo uses a stand 'to help us take good images.'
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The demo and commercial deployments happen in controlled indoor conditions; nobody on staff appears to own the government-fielding problem.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: No labels, no barcodes, no tags, no chips — just a photo from a standard camera, even a mobile phone.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Defense part fingerprint data is CUI/ITAR, but the support organization they are hiring is European
blind_spots.operator_reality: A registry of nuclear-component and Navy multi-die identities has to live on an accredited (IL4/IL5) enclave handled by US persons; their live openings put Senior Customer Engineers in Switzerland, Germany, and France, and no compliance, ISSO, or cleared-deployment role exists anywhere in the pipeline. The Phase II dies at the accreditation step regardless of how well the matching works.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Hiring mirrors the commercial European luxury/automotive pipeline, not the AFNWC transition path.

opener_hook: Alitheon's Phase II with the Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center (FA942222C0022) puts FeaturePrint's match registry inside CUI territory — yet the verify step still assumes the connectivity and phone policy of a Bellevue demo room, not a munitions depot.
what_they_do: Optical-AI 'fingerprinting' that identifies and authenticates individual physical parts from a photo of their surface micro-features, sold for anti-counterfeit and traceability.
